title: Millionaire's shortbread
summary: Almond shortbread, a soft allulose caramel and a snap of dark chocolate, stacked and cut into small squares.
steps: Heat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F). Line a 20 cm (8 in) square pan with parchment, leaving an overhang.
Mix the shortbread ingredients, press firmly into the pan and bake 15–18 minutes, until golden. Cool completely.

For the caramel, melt the butter with the allulose in a heavy pan and simmer, stirring, until it turns amber, 4–6 minutes. Pour in the cream carefully (it bubbles) and simmer 5–8 minutes more, stirring, until thick enough to coat a spoon. Stir in the vanilla and salt.
Pour the caramel over the cooled shortbread and chill 1 hour, until firm.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil, spread over the caramel and chill 1 hour more.
Let stand 10 minutes, then cut into 16 squares with a hot knife.
dairy_free_notes: The coconut-cream caramel is softer and tastes faintly of coconut; simmer it a few minutes longer and keep the bars in the fridge.
tips: Allulose caramel stays soft and chewy; erythritol would set gritty and hard.

origin.history: Caramel shortbread, a layer of caramel and chocolate on a shortbread base, is closely associated with Scotland, though when and where it was first made is not documented. The name millionaire's shortbread, a nod to its richness, became common in Britain in the later twentieth century.
